sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Caradawg was a Welsh hero. The Mabinogion name him a son of the king Brân the Blessed. Brân traveled to Ireland to wage war on the king who held Brânwen, Caradawg’s aunt, in an abusive marriage. Caradawg, still a youth, stayed behind as ruler of Wales. The usurper Caswallawn killed the royal retainers but spared Caradawg. Caradawg could not hold his father’s throne, and he died of heartbreak. Another Caradawg bore the names Freichfras (“of the strong arm”) and Briefbras (“short-armed”). Literature numbers this second Caradawg among the advisers to king Arthur.

okr.objective: Caradawg is a Welsh hero whose loss of his father’s throne ends in heartbreak.
